children.cond: Poor feeding, vomiting, lethargy, fever or low temperature, poor color

pill.text: Emergency department or admit now: blood culture, catheter urine culture, CSF if febrile or ill; glucose; INR; ammonia and lactate. IV antibiotics. IV acyclovir now if ALT is raised or INR prolonged — before the HSV PCR (dose per AAP Red Book and pharmacy). Sepsis, galactosemia, HSV and adrenal crisis until proved otherwise

children.cond: Liver failure in the first weeks — INR high, glucose low, ALT very high, or near-normal ALT with very high ferritin

pill.text: IV acyclovir now, before the HSV PCR (dose per AAP Red Book and pharmacy). Ferritin and AFP against the age norm. Think gestational alloimmune liver disease (GALD), HLH, metabolic disease — call a transplant center

children.cond: Vomiting on milk feeds, E. coli or other gram-negative sepsis, cataract, newborn screen pending — galactosemia possible

pill.text: Stop breast milk and lactose formula now, on suspicion — do not wait for results. Send urine reducing substances before the switch if it costs no time; red-cell GALT before any transfusion. Feed a galactose-free formula — soy-based, extensively hydrolyzed casein or elemental (GalNet 2017); sick after sucrose or fructose (HFI possible): elemental. Check glucose

children.cond: Active bleeding — umbilical stump, bruising, blood in stool or vomit, bulging fontanelle

pill.text: Emergency department / PICU: vitamin K IV now; head imaging if neurologic signs — vitamin K deficiency bleeding until proved otherwise
Vitamin K IV or subcutaneously now (confirm the infant dose with pharmacy); recheck INR the next day. Does not correct → liver failure: call a transplant center

children.cond: Hypoglycemia, micropenis, midline defects, roving eyes

pill.text: Hypopituitarism: draw the critical sample (cortisol, free T4, TSH) if it takes seconds, then treat the glucose — never delay glucose; endocrinology today; hydrocortisone before levothyroxine. Do not fast this infant for the ultrasound

children.cond: Contractures, renal tubular signs (ARC syndrome possible)

pill.text: No percutaneous liver biopsy — bleeding risk (ESPGHAN 2015). Diagnose by genes

children.text: Urinalysis, catheter urine culture and urine reducing substances — febrile or not.
Glucose. INR — if prolonged, parenteral vitamin K and recheck.
Newborn screen result. TSH and free T4 — a TSH-only screen misses central hypothyroidism.
Cortisol if hypoglycemic or any pituitary clue.
Before UDCA or a transfusion: urine bile acids (before UDCA), red-cell GALT (before transfusion).
Cholestasis confirmed: start fat-soluble vitamins from week 1, whatever the cause.

children.cond: All done and the infant is well

children.h: 3 · Stool first — atresia runs in parallel

children.text: Open a diaper and look yourself; use a stool color card. Pallor can come and go, and early atresia stools can look pigmented.

pill.text: Call pediatric hepatology and surgery today: biliary atresia until proved otherwise. INR and vitamin K; ultrasound and GGT the same day. No test may delay the cholangiogram

children.cond: Pigmented stools, direct or conjugated ≥ 1.0 mg/dL
children.subtext: Atresia is still possible — finish the parallel workup within one or two days

children.text: INR and parenteral vitamin K before any invasive step.
GGT, ALT, AST, ALP, albumin, CBC.

Abdominal ultrasound with Doppler: gallbladder, triangular cord, subcapsular flow, porta hepatis cyst, splenic malformation. Fasting 3–4 h unless hypoglycemia or hypopituitarism is possible. Tell the sonographer: rule out biliary atresia.
Alpha-1 antitrypsin level and Pi type. CMV IgM and blood or urine PCR — record it; it never delays the cholangiogram.
MMP-7 where a validated assay exists — read it against that lab's cut-off; it never overrides pale stools.
Sweat test or CFTR. Echo before the cholangiogram in any high-GGT infant; AP spine film and slit-lamp exam if any Alagille clue (murmur, face, posterior embryotoxon).
Genetic test with copy-number analysis, sent the same day — the result must not delay the cholangiogram.
Pale stools, absent or abnormal gallbladder, triangular cord, high GGT, high MMP-7 on a validated assay.
Do not order HIDA or wait for genetics — they cannot change this decision.

pill.text: Intraoperative cholangiogram, with Kasai under the same anesthetic, in an experienced center — this week

children.text: Pigmented stools but GGT high, or ultrasound normal.
Early biopsy can look like hepatitis: giant cells are common in atresia. A normal gallbladder does not exclude atresia.
HIDA only if biopsy is not available: excretion argues against atresia; non-excretion proves nothing. No phenobarbital priming.

pill.text: Liver biopsy within days, read by an experienced pediatric pathologist. Obstructive pattern → cholangiogram. Stools pale or bilirubin rising whatever the biopsy → cholangiogram

children.text: Pigmented stools, normal contracting gallbladder, low or normal GGT, low MMP-7 after the first month.
Low GGT: PFIC, bile acid synthesis defect (treatable) — urine bile acids before UDCA.
Alagille features: JAG1/NOTCH2 with copy number; no Kasai if the ducts are patent — a Kasai worsens Alagille outcomes.
Galactose or citrulline high: metabolic team (citrin deficiency, galactosemia). Succinylacetone high: tyrosinemia — metabolic team today.

children.cond: Another cause found or likely, and the infant is well

pill.text: Hepatology follow-up within 1–2 weeks with direct bilirubin and stool color. Stools turn pale or direct keeps rising → back to the cholangiogram

children.text: No age is too late for a Kasai if the liver is compensated: native-liver survival at 4 years was 23% after 90 days (Schreiber 2007).

children.cond: Compensated — no ascites, INR corrects with vitamin K

pill.text: Kasai still offered, this week, in an experienced center

children.cond: Ascites, INR not correcting, or established cirrhosis

pill.text: Transplant-center assessment before any Kasai (expert opinion)

children.cond: Fever, paler stools or rising bilirubin

pill.text: Cholangitis until proved otherwise: blood culture and IV antibiotics; admit

children.text: Track total bilirubin monthly for 3 months: below 2 mg/dL within 3 months means bile drainage (Superina 2011; Shneider 2016).

children.cond: Total bilirubin not below 2 mg/dL by 3 months, or any complication — growth failure, ascites, varices, recurrent cholangitis, hypoxemia

pill.text: Refer to a transplant center now — high risk of early progression (Shneider 2016); timing is expert opinion

children.text: Fat-soluble vitamins and nutrition from week 1.
